statement: You are given an undirected graph in which every edge has length 1: a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1), a list of edges [u, v], and a source vertex start.
Find the length of the shortest path from start to every vertex. Breadth-first search does this directly, because it reaches all vertices at distance d before any vertex at distance d + 1.
Return the distances as a list indexed by vertex, using −1 for a vertex that cannot be reached.

examples.explanation: Vertices 1 and 2 are neighbours of 0. Vertex 3 is two edges away by either route, and 4 and 5 follow along the tail.
Only the path 0 − 1 − 2 is connected to the source. Vertices 3 and 4 have no edges, so they are unreachable.
